findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile scope with the parent: either extend this leaf to also recover the tracked-deletion ('Your local changes ... would be overwritten by merge') abort class in push_recovery.py (parity with reconverge variant b), or update the parent epic's 'Push-recovery parity' decomposition line and split variant (b) into a named sibling ticket so the omission is explicit narrowing rather than an unowned gap.
evidence: Parent epic fb8a-7363-e406-4e36 child decomposition: 'Push-recovery parity (bug sulfuryl-suicidal-osprey): the non-fast-forward push recovery path gets the same untracked-collision + tracked-deletion recovery as reconverge.'

Leaf covers only variant (a): title '... leaves colliding untracked leftovers'; Approach moves only 'the named UNTRACKED colliding paths', parses only the '"untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge"' abort; every AC references only 'untracked-overwrite collisions'.

The tracked-deletion / local-changes-overwritten class (parent's variant b, handled in reconverge by sibling wolverine a560-85a8-1247-44cd in sync.py) is absent from the leaf's Scope, Testing and ACs.

No sibling ticket covers tracked-deletion recovery for push_recovery.py: the epic names a single push child (this one), and the wolverine sibling is scoped to src/rebar/_store/sync.py, not push_recovery.py.
ABSENCE rationale: with only variant (a) delivered and no sibling closing the variant (b) gap for push, the parent's stated 'push gets the same recovery as reconverge' goal provably cannot hold.
findings.finding: The leaf omits the tracked-deletion recovery that its parent's child-decomposition line explicitly assigns to it, and no sibling ticket covers that push case, so the parent's push-parity goal cannot fully hold.
findings.location: Whole plan (What/Approach/Scope/Acceptance Criteria) vs parent epic fb8a-7363-e406-4e36 child-decomposition line 'Push-recovery parity'
scenarios: An interrupted compaction fold leaves a STAGED/worktree tracked deletion (e.g. a *.retired rename's tracked-deletion half); a non-fast-forward push recovery merges the remote ref and git aborts with 'Your local changes ... would be overwritten by merge' — the push path still wedges and cannot self-heal, defeating the epic's push-parity goal.

findings.checklist_item: Use shutil.move (or a cross-device-safe move) rather than os.rename for the quarantine relocation, since the worktree and <git-common-dir> quarantine may be on different filesystems (EXDEV) — matching sync's _quarantine_untracked.
evidence: os.rename raises EXDEV across filesystems; git-common-dir and the worktree are not guaranteed co-located (worktrees, separate mounts)
Plan: 'os.rename against the same quarantine directory path'
findings.finding: The plan proposes moving colliding untracked files with os.rename, but the quarantine directory is under <git-common-dir> while the untracked file lives in the worktree. When those paths are on different filesystems (separate mount / tmpfs worktree / bind mount), os.rename raises OSError EXDEV. sync's proven mover deliberately uses shutil.move (which falls back to copy+unlink on EXDEV); os.rename does not.
findings.location: Approach — 'implement the quarantine move locally in push_recovery through core._git/os.rename'
scenarios: worktree on tmpfs or a mount distinct from the git-common-dir: the recovery move raises EXDEV and the retry never runs, re-wedging the push path the plan is trying to heal
findings.suggested_fix: Specify shutil.move for the local quarantine relocation (copy+unlink fallback on EXDEV), preserving byte-for-byte content, exactly as sync.py's _quarantine_untracked does.

findings.checklist_item: Resolve the dir-path helper seam: either resolve the quarantine dir locally in push_recovery via core._git (not sync's _git), or confirm 1767 exposes a git-injectable dir helper — do not 'share' _quarantine_dir as-is since it shells through sync's un-patched module-level _git.
evidence: Plan: 'every push_recovery function deliberately late-binds core._git so push's ~25-site test monkeypatch keeps working'; 'implement the quarantine move locally in push_recovery through core._git … rather than calling sync's mover across the seam'
The dir-path helper contains a subprocess through sync's _git identical in kind to the mover's — sharing it contradicts the stated seam constraint
findings.finding: The plan proposes to 'share the dir-path helper if 1767 exposes one', but the exposed helper (_quarantine_dir) resolves the git-common-dir by shelling `rev-parse --git-common-dir` through sync's module-level _git — the very cross-seam subprocess the plan says push_recovery must avoid (it late-binds core._git so push's ~25-site monkeypatch keeps working). Sharing that helper re-introduces the monkeypatch-escape for the dir-resolution git call.
findings.location: Approach — 'share the dir-path helper if 1767 exposes one'
scenarios: push_recovery calls sync._quarantine_dir under a test that monkeypatches push._git: the rev-parse runs REAL git against the tracker while the test asserts on the fake
git-common-dir resolution diverges from the merge/reset git calls that go through core._git
findings.suggested_fix: State that the quarantine-dir path is computed locally in push_recovery using core._git for `rev-parse --git-common-dir` (mirroring the local mover), reusing only the pure path-composition logic (or a helper 1767 exposes that accepts an injected git runner), not sync._quarantine_dir's subprocess.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the partial-move failure behavior: if an os.rename in the quarantine sequence fails after moving some files, define whether the already-moved paths are rolled back (or documented as recoverable from the timestamped quarantine dir) before falling through to abort/restore-stash.
evidence: Plan: 'move the named UNTRACKED colliding paths into the shared quarantine directory ... retry the merge ONCE; any other failure keeps today's behavior exactly (abort, restore stash, warn or strict-raise).'

The stash restore covers TRACKED edits only; untracked files already moved to quarantine are not part of the stash, so a mid-move failure could leave them stranded in quarantine with no recorded recovery.
findings.finding: The quarantine move step (multiple os.rename calls of named untracked paths) has no stated behavior for a PARTIAL failure: if the move succeeds for some named paths then fails mid-sequence (permission, race, or an os.rename error), the plan's 'any other failure keeps today's behavior exactly (abort, restore stash)' does not say whether already-moved files are moved back, leaving a partially-quarantined worktree while the stash is restored.
findings.location: Approach — 'move the named UNTRACKED colliding paths into the shared quarantine directory ... any other failure keeps today's behavior exactly'
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Testing/Approach note: on any move error, the already-moved paths remain in the timestamped quarantine subdir (recoverable, bytes preserved) and the path then falls through to the existing abort+restore-stash; add a test asserting the partial-move case restores the stash and leaves moved bytes recoverable in quarantine.
